title: Balanced Training Scroll
statement:
A dojo training scroll is written with the bracket characters `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}`. Given a string `s` of just these characters, return True if every bracket is properly closed in the correct order.

Constraints:
- 0 <= len(s) <= 10^4
- s consists only of the characters ()[]{}
hint: Push every opening bracket onto a stack. On a closing bracket, it must match whatever is currently on top of the stack — pop it if so, otherwise the scroll is unbalanced.

title: Echoing Chant
statement:
A ranger's chant `s` cancels itself: any two adjacent identical letters vanish, and this repeats until no adjacent pair remains. Return the final chant.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(s) <= 10^5
- s consists of lowercase English letters
hint: Walk the string with a stack: if the top of the stack matches the current letter, pop it (they cancel); otherwise push the letter.

title: The Featherweight Pack
statement:
A ranger's gear pack supports `push(x)`, `pop()`, `top()`, and `getMin()` (all must run in O(1) time). You're given a list of operations to simulate in order on a single pack, where each operation is `["push", x]`, `["pop"]`, `["top"]`, or `["getMin"]`. Return a list with one entry per operation: the returned value for `"top"`/`"getMin"`, and `None` for `"push"`/`"pop"`.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(ops) <= 200
- pop, top, and getMin are never called on an empty pack
hint: Keep a normal stack, plus a second 'running minimum' stack that pushes the smaller of (new value, its own current top) alongside every push, and pops in lockstep — its top is always the min of what's currently in the main stack.

title: Order Through the Gate
statement:
The dojo master wants trainee orders relayed first-come-first-served (FIFO), but the gate only has two stacks to work with. Given operations `["push", x]`, `["pop"]`, `["peek"]`, or `["empty"]`, simulate a queue built from two stacks and return the result of each operation in order (`None` for `"push"`).

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(ops) <= 100
- pop and peek are never called on an empty queue
hint: Push new orders onto an 'in' stack. When you need to pop or peek, if the 'out' stack is empty, dump the entire 'in' stack into it first — that reverses it back into FIFO order.

title: Decoding the Command Scroll
statement:
A ranger battle command is written in postfix (Reverse Polish) notation: a list of tokens where each token is either an integer or one of `+ - * /`. Evaluate it and return the result. Division truncates toward zero.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(tokens) <= 10^4
- Each token is an integer or one of + - * /
hint: Push numbers onto a stack. On an operator, pop the top two values (second-popped is the left operand), apply the operator, and push the result back.

title: Awaiting a Stronger Rival
statement:
A ranger records a rival's power level each day, `levels`. For every day, find how many days must pass until a strictly stronger rival appears; if none ever does, that day gets 0.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(levels) <= 10^5
- 0 <= levels[i] <= 100
hint: Keep a stack of day-indices whose 'stronger rival' is still unresolved. Whenever today's level beats the level at the top index, that index's answer is (today - that index); pop and repeat.

title: Scouting the Next Rival
statement:
You scout a sequence of rival power levels `nums2` (all distinct). For each value in a shorter watch-list `nums1` (every value in `nums1` also appears somewhere in `nums2`), find the next strictly greater level appearing to its right in `nums2`; use -1 if none exists.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(nums1) <= len(nums2) <= 1000
- All values in nums2 are distinct; every value in nums1 also appears in nums2
hint: Scan nums2 once with a stack of values still waiting for their next-greater. Whenever the current value beats the stack's top, that's its answer — pop and repeat, then push the current value.

title: Banner Formations
statement:
Given `n` pairs of dojo banners, return every combination of well-formed (properly nested and balanced) parenthesis sequences that can be made using exactly `n` pairs.

Constraints:
- 1 <= n <= 8
hint: Build the sequence one character at a time with backtracking: you may add '(' whenever you've used fewer than n so far, and ')' only when it wouldn't outnumber the '(' already placed.

title: Clashing Projectiles
statement:
A row of ranger energy blasts moves along a single line. A positive value moves right, a negative value moves left, and its absolute value is its size. When two blasts moving toward each other meet, the smaller is destroyed; if equal, both are destroyed. Blasts moving the same direction never meet. Return the sizes/directions remaining after all collisions resolve.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(blasts) <= 10^4
- Every value is a nonzero integer
hint: Process left to right with a stack of survivors moving right. A new leftward blast only fights the stack's top if that top is moving right; keep resolving collisions with the top until it's destroyed, the new blast is destroyed, or there's nothing left to fight.

title: The Widest Training Mat
statement:
BOSS TRIAL — A row of stacked training pillars has heights `heights`. Find the area of the largest rectangle that can be formed from a contiguous run of pillars, where the rectangle's height is limited by the shortest pillar included.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(heights) <= 10^5
- 0 <= heights[i] <= 10^4
hint: Keep a stack of indices with increasing heights. When a shorter pillar appears, pop and finalize rectangles using each popped height as the limiting height, with width spanning back to the new stack top.
